correctness.rationale: The finite, specifically defined GP(10,2) perfect-matching subcomplex was independently reconstructed from the 30 sorted graph edges and all 36 perfect matchings. Downward closure has 30,504 faces including empty, with cardinality f-vector (1,30,375,2180,5790,8352,7440,4320,1620,360,36). The coordinate-order acyclic matching has 15,231 pairs and exactly one 0-, ten 2-, and thirty 3-cells; the audited verifier checks all 163,650 Hasse incidences by topological sorting. Signed gradient-path recurrence on the original boundary gives a 10x30 integral matrix with 34 negative, 231 zero and 35 positive entries. Independent rank calculations find rank_F2=9 and rank_F3=10; independent Bareiss determinant of the specified maximal minor (columns 0,2,4,5,6,7,8,10,11,26) equals +2. Thus Smith factors are nine units and one factor 2. With one 0-cell, no 1-cells and only 2/3-cells, Hurewicz pi_2=H_2 identifies all 3-cell attachment classes and Smith moves yield M(Z/2,2) wedge twenty S^3, not merely matching mod-2 Betti numbers. No assertion about all cubic graphs is used.

value.rationale: The perfect-matching complex of a standard polyhedral cubic graph is a natural object already studied in the literature. Detecting and completely locating integral 2-torsion in its homotopy type supplies an exact, reusable non-sphere-wedge example not implied by counting its perfect matchings or by ordinary matching-complex homology. A full finite model and integer attaching matrix make the precise fact independently useful.

limitations: Only GP(10,2) and the perfect-matching subcomplex, no equivariant homotopy or extension to all cubic graphs.
